settings_schema.header:
## Channel Requests

Lets non-admins **request** things instead of creating them directly: channels, teams, Team Admin rights, incoming webhooks, and bot tokens. Use the per-type toggles below to control what users can request. Requests are posted to the approval channel; System Admins (and optionally Team Admins) can approve or deny.

Webhook and bot-token requests use **two-step approval** — one security approver and one system approver, identified by the User Attributes named below. Pick the approval team + channel via the dropdowns, then configure domain prefixes so channels follow your naming convention automatically.

settings.help_text: When enabled, users can request the creation of new channels. Turn this off to hide the channel-request entry points and reject channel-request submissions.
When enabled, members can request that someone be promoted to Channel Admin on an existing channel. Turn this off to hide the "Request Channel Admin" menu item and reject its submissions.
When enabled, users can request the creation of new teams for admin approval.
When enabled, users can request incoming webhooks for a channel, delivered privately once approved.
When enabled, users can request Team Admin promotion on a team they belong to, for admin approval.
When enabled, users can request a bot token. Bot token requests require two-step approval (a security approver and a system approver).

Name of the User Attribute (in the access_control group) that marks a user as a security-step approver for two-step requests. A user with a non-empty value for this attribute may approve the security step. Manage the attribute and its values in System Console → User Management → Attributes.

Name of the User Attribute (in the access_control group) that marks a user as a system/admin-step approver for two-step requests. A user with a non-empty value for this attribute may approve the system step.
Dropdown of teams you're a member of. Pick the team containing your approval channel.
Dropdown of channels in the selected team. Pick the channel where new channel requests get posted for approval.

Structured editor: define allowed channel prefixes (team-, project-, etc.) with descriptions and suffix rules. Requesters pick from a dropdown; the resulting channel URL is prefix+suffix. Includes preset packs for common org shapes and a live preview.
When enabled, Team Admins of the approval team can click Approve/Deny in addition to System Admins.
Tab-complete picker: pick users whose channel requests bypass approval and create the channel immediately. Useful for delegated managers.
When set, every approve/deny action logs a message to this channel. Useful for compliance.
